name: Press & Media
description: Press and media outreach as injectable behaviour: a provider registry, five adapter shapes (free submission, PR wire, media database, ad platform, direct I/O), and the factual-discipline kernel that stops generated copy inventing products, people, quotes or statistics. The buyer supplies AI, email, notification and HTTP through ports, and brings their own provider accounts.
_payloadRoot: Three roots. press-media-core is the portable; portable-kernel carries company identity and factual discipline; portable-audit carries the SIEM event shape. The core reaches both by relative path, so all three must ship or a buyer's extraction has broken imports.
_minModules: Walked on 2026-07-26: 15 modules — 9 core, 3 kernel, 3 audit. A materially shorter walk means an entry point moved or an adapter stopped being reachable from the barrel.
_hostFallbacks: Empty, and verified empty by a real graph walk: this portable's buyer surface has NO bare or aliased imports at all. Everything it needs arrives through ports. If the gate ever reports one, something host-coupled was added to the core.
_knownNamingExceptions: Empty and verified empty. Keep it that way — the build platform's name must not reach a buyer's records.
buyerMustSupply: AiPort — generates campaign creative. The buyer's model, the buyer's key, the buyer's spend. The payload contains no provider SDK.
EmailPort — sends a release to a recipient. Display name and signature come from the company record, so a buyer's outreach never arrives under another company's name.
OwnerNotifyPort — tells a human what the engine did or wants approved.
HttpPort — optional. Required only by adapters that call a provider API directly.
RunnerPort — optional. Config-driven execution for paid providers; without it, paid adapters have no transport.

CompanyProfilePort — optional but strongly recommended. It is how the engine knows whose company it is writing for; without it, generated copy carries visible [PLACEHOLDER] markers instead of invented facts.
Provider accounts and credentials — PR wire, media database or ad platform accounts are the buyer's, billed to the buyer.
notIncluded: Any press, wire, media-database or advertising account. The portable knows the shape of those providers; the relationship is the buyer's.
An AI provider or model. Generation happens through the buyer's AiPort.
An email transport. The payload composes; the buyer's EmailPort delivers.
A datastore. Campaign persistence belongs to the buyer's host layer.
Any credential. Nothing in the archive contains or requires a build-platform account.
Scheduling, retries or queueing. The buyer's host decides when the engine runs.
supportedPlatforms: TypeScript 5.x, non-strict and strict both compile
Any AI provider reachable through the buyer's AiPort
Any email transport reachable through the buyer's EmailPort
Any SIEM accepting ECS-JSON or CEF, via the bundled audit module
No native modules, no runtime dependencies of any kind

upgradeCompatibility.policy: Within 1.x the port interfaces (AiPort, EmailPort, OwnerNotifyPort, HttpPort, RunnerPort, CompanyProfilePort) change additively only. A new required member on any of them is a major version. New adapters and new exports are minor.
upgradeCompatibility.adapterRegistry: Adapters are registered at runtime by the host. A buyer's own adapter implementing MediaProviderAdapter continues to work across minor versions.
upgradeCompatibility.rollback: The payload holds no state. Rolling back is restoring the previous archive and repointing imports.

knownLimitations: Factual discipline is enforced by prompt construction and by visible [PLACEHOLDER] markers, not by a post-generation checker. A buyer should still review copy before it reaches a journalist.
Paid adapters (PR wire, media database, ad platform) require a RunnerPort; without one they can describe what they need but cannot dispatch.
Proof collection is provider-shaped and asynchronous. A dispatch returning 'submitted' is not evidence of publication.
Seats and execution limits in a licence are contract terms, not enforced controls.

acceptance._note: No acceptance harness exists for this portable yet. Unlike the Self-Healing Supervisor, whose safety property demands one, this portable's risk is commercial rather than operational — but a buyer still needs proof it works against their own ports before they trust it with a journalist. Build one before dropping -rc.
